summary.headline: The Personnel Board approved FY27 municipal pay rates but split 2-2 on an extra raise for an employee at the top step.
summary.summary: The Southborough Personnel Board approved FY27 wage rates for municipal employees while addressing delays in annual performance evaluations submitted by department heads. A motion to grant an additional 2 percent pay increase to a longtime employee who has exceeded Step 15 failed on a 2-2 tie vote, with members deciding to await the results of an upcoming classification study. Staff also reported that the contract for the comprehensive salary study has been finalized with consultant MGT, with a project kickoff anticipated in early July.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The board approved the meeting minutes from May 29, 2026, complimenting the new line-item formatting, and later adjourned the meeting.
key_details: Approved May 29, 2026 meeting minutes
Praise noted for line-numbered meeting minute format
Adjourned meeting by roll call vote

topics.title: Personnel transition and staffing report
topics.summary: Staff reported stable municipal staffing with no departures or new hires to report for the preceding month. The board was informed that an upcoming vacancy will be advertised soon.
key_details: No staff transitions or turnover reported for the month
A part-time position in the Town Clerk office will be posted after July 4

topics.title: Comprehensive salary study contract update
topics.summary: Staff announced that the contract with consultant MGT for the town-wide salary and classification study was finalized and ready for signature. The board discussed arrangements for an all-employee kickoff session, expressing a preference for the consultant to attend in person.
key_details: Contract returned from consultant MGT for execution by the town administrator
Kickoff meeting for employees and board members targeted for late June or right after July 4
Board requested an in-person kickoff presentation rather than a fully remote meeting
Study is expected to review the town 15-step compensation grid
topics.outcome: Contract executed; staff to schedule kickoff meeting

topics.title: Proposed pay adjustment for employee exceeding step schedule
topics.summary: The board debated whether to grant an additional 2 percent step increase outside the grid to a longtime employee who reached the top step and was otherwise only slated for a 3 percent cost-of-living adjustment. Proponents argued the employee should receive the 5 percent total increase other staff receive, while opposing members maintained the board should wait for the comprehensive salary study before making exceptions.
key_details: Addressed pay for an employee who has exceeded Step 15
Motion proposed adding a 2 percent off-grid increase to equal the 5 percent raise received by staff moving up steps
Staff noted several additional employees will reach the Step 15 ceiling over the next couple of years
Motion failed on a 2-2 tie vote

topics.title: FY27 employee pay rates and performance review compliance
topics.summary: The board reviewed and approved proposed FY27 wage rates for municipal staff, holding over one pending library review. During the discussion, a board member strongly criticized department heads who submit performance evaluations late, noting that tardy reviews jeopardize employees receiving their scheduled July 1 raises.
key_details: Approved FY27 municipal wage rates as presented, including a late-submitted rate sheet for Debbie Moore
One review for a library employee was deferred to the next meeting
Town performance reviews are due annually by the first Wednesday in June
Board discussed sending a formal letter to department heads demanding timely completion of reviews
topics.why_it_matters: Authorizes annual wage adjustments across town departments and determines whether staff receive scheduled pay increases on time.

topics.title: Discussion of agenda deadlines and minutes posting
topics.summary: The chair proposed establishing an informal practice of submitting agenda items five business days prior to meetings, though members noted open meeting law requires 48 hours and the chair already controls the agenda. The board also reviewed timelines for delivering approved minutes to the town clerk for website publication.
key_details: Chair suggested a 5-day cutoff for new agenda items
State open meeting law mandates agenda posting at least 48 hours in advance
Town bylaws allow up to 45 days to file approved minutes
Staff clarified that draft minutes can be submitted if needed to meet statutory deadlines
topics.outcome: Discussion only; no formal policy changes adopted

topics.title: Summer meeting calendar planning
topics.summary: Board members reviewed their availability and vacation schedules for July and August. Staff agreed to circulate a scheduling poll to establish summer meeting dates.
key_details: Member absences noted for mid-July and mid-August
Staff will distribute a poll covering potential dates in both July and August
topics.outcome: Staff to send scheduling poll to members

votes.motion: Grant an additional 2 percent pay increase outside the grid to an employee who exceeded Step 15
Approve the FY27 pay rates for town positions as presented

upcoming.what: Kickoff meeting with MGT for town salary and classification study
Town Clerk office part-time position job posting
Personnel Board consideration of pending library employee FY27 pay rate
